why: Split by what each byte's context offers (gap_by_piece_test.json, gap_by_piece_validation.json), the v16 stack is ahead of the Transformer of its size and training wherever the eight bytes before a target can be copied (0.09 bits a byte from the last 2 KB, 0.32 from 2 to 8 KB back) and behind on new contexts by 0.057 to 0.066, on three quarters of the bytes: the whole gap is knowledge, not memory. The stack spends 41% of its parameters on its reads (tags, probes, payloads and projections) against the Transformer's 33% on attention, and 58% on its cells against 66% on the MLPs. On the test bed, knowledge cells gain on copyable bytes (0.036) and nothing on new ones, which is why they do not help at full size.
question: Does moving parameters from the reads to the cells, at equal parameters, buy knowledge (bits on new contexts) for memory (bits on copyable bytes), and is the trade worth making?

arms.r128: reads 128 wide (four heads of 32 channels) and 1,342 cells a level: 5,250,980 parameters
arms.r384: reads 384 wide (four heads of 96 channels) and 702 cells a level: 5,247,140 parameters, the other way

reference: combo-bed of knowledge_and_plasticity.json: the delayed test bed (reads 256 wide, 1,022 cells, 5,249,060 parameters) trained the same way: the same code, flags, seed 20001, data order and device; every arm differs only in --read-width and --granule-cells
training: On streams (--stream 10 --stream-groups 3), 6,000 updates, on the server's CPU, as combo-bed
measure: The first 2,000,000 bytes of the enwik8 validation split as 16 unbroken streams (lead 8,192, pieces of 512), as trained and with v15's rule on all six levels at 2^22, with the bits of every piece kept, combo-bed scored again with its bits. Each arm against combo-bed is split by what the context offers (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 256 bytes, the bed's reach, and far 8,192): the gain on new contexts and on copyable bytes.
reading: The trade buys knowledge if r128 gains on new contexts with the 95% interval above zero, and r384 is expected to lose there. It is worth making if r128 is also ahead of combo-bed overall, as trained and with v15's rule, by at least 0.010: then four seeds, and a full-size stack with narrower reads and more cells. One seed per arm: a screen.
seen_before_recording: The gap split of the v16 pair and of the test bed's knowledge and kept cells; no stack with another read width at equal parameters has been trained.
